name: llmc_attention_backward
goal: Port attention_backward_harness.cu (llm.c dev/cuda/attention_backward.cu, fp32 build) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers. Keep every kernel variant k in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] as its own SYCL kernel, computed on the SYCL device, and keep the program's contract: `build/candidate <input> <output> B T C NH` reads the inputs and writes each variant's outputs in order as raw float32, exactly as the CUDA main does. A hidden reference checks the output (atol 0.001 + rtol FLT_EPSILON*|ref|, llm.c's own fp32 rule). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources: migrate's output under migrated/ counts, so delete it (delete_file) once your own port is done. migrate's output can be long: read it in parts (read_file offset/limit) or work from the CUDA harness. cuBLAS calls go to oneMath (oneapi::math::blas, #include <oneapi/math.hpp>; the compile flags already link -lonemath), not to oneapi::mkl product APIs. Use oneapi::math::blas::column_major, as cuBLAS itself is column-major (swap the operands for row-major data): oneMath's cuBLAS backend does not implement row_major, so a row_major call aborts on NVIDIA GPUs even though it runs on the CPU.

museport.note: B=2, T=256 (llm.c: B=4, T=1024); C=768, NH=12 as in llm.c. T stays a multiple of the block size 256, as llm.c's is: variant 6 writes up to the next multiple of the block size in each row, so with T=128 it writes into the next row. att is zeroed before the forward pass, which writes only its lower triangle; variant 6 reads the upper one (in llm.c it is fresh cudaMalloc memory). dinp, the gradient llm.c checks last, is compared at llm.c's 1e-3. As in llm.c, the backward pass runs on the GPU forward pass's buffers and the CPU reference on the CPU forward pass's; the scratch gradients are zeroed before each variant, since the kernels accumulate. cuBLAS runs in fp32 (CUBLAS_DEFAULT_MATH).
